summary: Verified Google Maps loading fix on /formerchants LocationPicker. Map tiles render, marker placement/reverse-geocoding works, Confirm Location returns coordinates to the merchant form. No BillingNotEnabledMapError, no 'For development purposes only' watermark, no map error dialog.

issues: Business location field is populated with raw coordinates '28.614371, 77.209000' after Confirm rather than the formatted address shown in the picker. Consider passing the reverse-geocoded address string for better UX.

action_items: Optional: On Confirm, populate businessLocation with the human-readable address (already computed as 'Selected Location:' text) instead of only lat/lng.
Optional deprecations: google.maps.Marker deprecated -> AdvancedMarkerElement; google.maps.places.SearchBox unavailable to new customers -> migrate to PlaceAutocompleteElement.
critical_code_review_comments: API key is exposed publicly in frontend build (unavoidable for Maps JS) — ensure HTTP referrer restrictions + API restrictions are configured on the Google Cloud key to prevent quota abuse.
LocationPicker uses polling for window.google.maps; consider using the official callback (already set as initMap in index.html) or @googlemaps/js-api-loader for cleaner load handling.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Google Maps billing issue is resolved. REACT_APP_GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY loads correctly. Map renders in LocationPicker with tiles; click-to-place marker works; Confirm fills businessLocation with coordinates. Only console warnings observed are Google's deprecation notices for Marker and places.SearchBox (informational, non-blocking) and expected 'Geolocation error' (headless, denied permission — falls back to Delhi default as designed).
rca of the issue: Original bug: BillingNotEnabledMapError due to hardcoded API key without billing. Fix: env var REACT_APP_GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY with billing-enabled key injected via %REACT_APP_GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY% in public/index.html. Verified: no billing/key errors in console; map + tiles render successfully.
